_comment: Every Slither finding over contracts/src must match one entry (check + Contract.function, or '*' for every location of that check, with the exact `count` of locations, so a new location fails the run); script/slither_report.py fails on an unmatched finding or an entry that no longer matches anything. Verdicts: fixed | false-positive | accepted. The v1 core (MethaneCovenant, KeyRegistry) is byte-identical by rule (make core-bytecode), so its findings can only be explained.

entries.reason: Equality of organisation ids (`org == bytes32(0)`, `org == sellerOrg || org == buyerOrg`) read from the registry; no balance or timestamp is compared, nothing an attacker can nudge by one unit.
`seen[j] == org` is the distinct-organisation check of the quorum; ids, not amounts.
Role and organisation-id comparisons (seller and buyer must be different organisations); ids, not amounts.
Zero-id / zero-address / NONE-role input validation; ids and enums, not amounts.
Same input validation as the v1 registry plus `role == OBSERVER`; ids and enums, not amounts.

`amount == 0` on the contract's own balance only decides `NothingToWithdraw`; ETH forced in (selfdestruct) simply becomes withdrawable by the funder, which is the intended owner of everything the contract holds (test_suretyBond_withdraw_* in test/unit/SuretyBond.t.sol).
`bool dup;` relies on the language default `false` and is set inside the inner loop; test_quorumNotMet_twoKeysSameOrg_reverts (test/unit/MethaneCovenant.t.sol) pins the behaviour.

`PoolVerify.cleanQuorum` returns the distinct signing orgs, which `attestCleanPass` stores for the observer fee; a resolution pays no fee (D11), so here the call is made for its checks only: it reverts unless k distinct independent orgs signed the same claim, scene and kind (test_resolvePass_* in test/unit/IncentivePool.t.sol).

One `registry.keyStatus` view call per attestation, to the covenant's immutable KeyRegistry (set in the constructor, no admin after renounce), bounded by MAX_ATTESTATIONS = 16; a reverting registry would only stop that transaction (fail closed).

SuretyBond has no mutable storage (four immutables); the callee is the immutable core, and the event needs the covenant id the call returns. Nothing a re-entrant call could reorder in this contract's state (test/unit/HostileReceiver.t.sol covers re-entry on the payout paths).

No mutable storage; the callees are the immutable core and pool, whose `withdraw` zero the credit before sending (checks-effects-interactions). The event reports the amounts those calls moved, so it must follow them.
No mutable storage; the callee is the immutable registry (`revokeKey` on this contract's own key). The event follows the revocation it reports.

Every flagged comparison orders `block.timestamp` against windows of hours to years (challenge, contest, clean, resolve, hold windows, key validity, proposal TTL, term end). Validator drift of seconds cannot move an outcome across a window edge that matters, and no equality on time is used. The same lint is disabled in foundry.toml for this reason.

The three `withdraw()` pull payments (core, pool, SuretyBond) send ETH with `call` after zeroing the credit; a failed send reverts and keeps the credit (test/unit/HostileReceiver.t.sol: reentrant and reverting receivers on core and pool).
`DOMAIN_SEPARATOR()` is the EIP-712 / EIP-2612 conventional name off-chain signers look for.
